steps.text: A few days later...
Stitch is working hard at the forum again today.
Just like the journey to the surface, the dressing of the city is a task that requires the supervision of all the citizens.
And as the face of the city, the dome's renovation is naturally the most important task.
Which is why it is also necessary for the design tasks to be done in the forum, where everyone can see.
And as Master Edge claims, it also saves time.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: That darned old man. He's definitely having me do this because he thinks it's funny.
Noticing Edge's smug look below, Stitch finds himself immediately incensed.
However, not even he himself expected to adapt so quickly to these work conditions.
When he has to take questions from passersby, when he has to hear opinions, and even when he stands up and defends his beliefs in an argument—
None of that actually carries as much pressure as he thought it would.
With Edge grinning away at him, Stitch is definitely irritated, but he also knows what people must be thinking about him.
Just like how they must know what he is thinking.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: This little runt. He's had more arguments than I could count the past few days.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Just because someone dared to give him some feedback, he had to argue for the better part of the day.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Still, the work he's turning in is impeccable.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Finch, I don't know where in the world you've tromped off to, but you can rest easy now.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Oh, right, right.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Stitch!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: What is it? I'm working here!

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Somebody found a letter at the top of the dome while it was being inspected.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: A letter?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Yep, and it's for you.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: No way...!

a.text: I am Finch Canvas, the Zeruertza's greatest architectural designer.
I placed this letter at the top of the dome.
I am sure the one who opens it will be the next person to renovate it.
I hope that he is my dearest student.
This letter is for him.
However, if you are not him, then please do not give him this letter.
As that would mean he has failed.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Sorry, Catch.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: If only I were more like you...

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Everyone's personality is different, and I can understand the way you think, too.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: All I can say is, if I'd found out a little sooner, maybe things could've turned out different.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: You're allowed to stay, you know.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: *Sigh*, it feels like I did something terrible to you.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Not at all, Elysium. I really appreciate your suggestion.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: It's true that I made this decision to give him that push at first, but I also really want to seek out Master Finch.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I'm sure he'll be very happy to hear how Stitch is doing.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Well, you've made it plenty hard for me to know what to say here.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Speaking of which, it sounds like this Master Finch really cares about his student. I have a hunch that he might have gone to the surface to seek a cure for Oripathy.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: After I leave, I will try my best to track him down, too.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hah, perhaps he will one day find his way to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Oh, now there's a plan.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You know what I'm trying to say, right?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Yeah, we'll meet again.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I know I want to help out when we finally rebuild Zeruertza.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: And when the time comes, I am going to work together with Stitch to put out some amazing designs.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Like a statue of me?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Well... Maybe not that.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: A shame!

a.text: First, I must apologize to you for my departure.
But if I had not left, knowing you, you would never become truly independent.
Alright, truth be told, if I decided to stay, I wouldn't have known how to stop caring for you.
You have a gift.
Oripathy has greatly limited your lifespan, but at the same time, it has made you see life in a more profound way.
Thanks to this, your style has greatly transformed for the better.
I can tell.

steps.name: Excited Archosauria
steps.text: Here we go, let's pull it together. Our job today is the blow all the caverns in this area!

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: You hear that, Yogi?

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: Yes, Brother!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: *yawn*, Yota, did you have to start working this early?

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: What are you talking about, Inam?

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: This is a mission Gavial gave us herself.

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: She saved my life. If I could, I would dig through the earth to meet her right now and check how she's been doing.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: She'll still be alive and kicking, well after you're dead.

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: Haha, that's for sure.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Right, I'll be leaving tomorrow to meet the Pasha and discuss the lord ameer business.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: So, starting tomorrow, Zumama's in charge. Got it?

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: How about I come with you, then?

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: Didn't you say the Pasha is a pain to deal with?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: For you, yeah. The Pasha would grind you until there's nothing left.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Don't worry. I haven't been a Messenger all these years for nothing.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Alright, Zumama, I'll leave this to you.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Don't worry.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: We've installed the 'Mountain Breaker Mk. III' on the Raging Ironhide.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: That'll put its efficiency up three-fold.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: You could even leave me this whole place.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Sometimes... I feel like you're even scarier than Gavial.

a.text: At the same time, this has made your style more and more extreme.
And the more you stood firm with your style, the more you despised working with others.
This worried me.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: By the way, Avdotya. What are you going to do once you make it to the surface?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: What else can I do?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: You can't believe I will settle down for a life on land just because of the speech I gave?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Once Zeruertza is rebuilt, I will be back.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Is there a problem?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Right... Actually, this only just came back to me, but I made a promise to Inam.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: We agreed that if I ever went to the surface, I would do business with her, and she would also introduce me to a place called Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: But I don't know that much about the surface, so I told her you would be our middleman, and I could learn from you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: So that means...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: You sold me to her?!

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: I'm sorry! But I really want to try doing business on the surface. Please, help me out!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Croooooque! Diamondfaaaaaaaace!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Didn't I tell you not to drink?!

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: I'm really, really sorry!

a.text: When aloofness yields no result, it only devolves into misconception.
It tells you that it isn't your fault that others don't understand you. It tells you that others are in the wrong for not understanding your work.
But sometimes, that couldn't be further from the truth.
You can of course hold on to the way you think.
However, if your line of thought is really so fine and exquisite, shouldn't you try your best to share it all the more?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Phew, this pillar will look just fine here.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I didn't expect them to want to renovate the forum, too. The Durins are a thorough bunch, aren't they?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Gavial.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Do you realize that you are making history?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Is that right?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: The Durins have lived underground for ages without making any large-scale effort at communicating with the world on the surface.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Yet your choices have persuaded an entire city to relocate to the surface all at once.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Who would have thought that Acahualla would be the first place to know such an intimate level of exchange with a Durin city and its people?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: And when future generations look back, it will probably never occur to them that this all happened because of an offhand idea you came up with.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Now that you mention it, I guess you're right.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But there's nothing wrong with that, is there?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Haha, there's of course nothing wrong with that.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: What I'm saying is—History is always like that, Gavial.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: It might have been an accident that the Durins were able to put down roots underground, too.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: This goes to show that perhaps history is nothing to be revered or feared, just like the Acahuallan traditions that you so easily destroyed.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Now I'm not so sure about that. I think people who know their history pretty great.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Like Dr. Kal'tsit. She knows history like the back of her hand.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Kal'tsit? Hm... I could count the number of times we've dealt with each other on one hand, but she might be the one person in the whole world who takes history the lightest.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Is that right?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Of course. And I suspect the way she goes about it might even be a kind of helplessness, the kind that comes from knowing nothing can be done.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Now then, let's change the subject.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Zumama told me that you wavered in your decision, but you persisted with it nonetheless, and that you plan to continue doing as much?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah, I mean, they all told me that they'll help me.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Speaking of, you're gonna stick with us till the end, right, old man?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Oh, look at you, won't even give an old man a break.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: It's probably obvious that I'm very happy to be researching technology with Zumama.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: But did you know that the longer you live, the harder it is to find direction?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'm not sure I get it.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Well, that's good. That's what I like about you.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Keep going down the path you're on. I'm curious just how far you'll make it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So, how come you're here to talk to me instead of following Zumama around?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Well, naturally, that's because—

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: She kicked me out!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I told her the Durin machines are nowhere near as cute as the Big, Ugly Thing, and she got mad at me.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Hmph, how could she be this protective of her new friends? Now I'm mad too!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh.

a.text: There are certain things that you will never understand until you experience them yourself.
And so I am leaving you with a problem.
Until you become the next design representative,
and until you manage to persuade all of Zeruertza that your work has a profound meaning within...
I will leave your side, and you are not allowed to come look for me.
We are architects, and our job is to provide designs that satisfy the masses.
You will come to understand that this is the greatest challenge you will ever face. Not a design flaw, not a construction problem, but rather something as simple as being persuasive.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Whoa, Tomimi, you feel that?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Yeah, it's shaking.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'm surprised we can still feel it even though we've taken the lift all the way up here.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Those are some huge tremors.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: But all the Zeruertzans have made it to the surface. Every last one of them!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah, everyone's done a great job.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Hrrrhhh...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You okay? I told you to drop the tough act, but you had to be the last one to leave the city.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What inspiration can you get from watching it crumble anyway?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: You wouldn't understand, even if I told you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: That was the final moment of an entire city. It simply... overwhelmed me with emotion.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Master... This might be impossibly difficult, but I will give it my best shot.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: And you, little whelp. What are you mumbling to yourself?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: He... He looks exhausted.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Well, can you blame him? He's been working really hard.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Not only did he actually manage to design the thing, he went to the construction site every day, and even insisted on being the last one out.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: A while back, I wouldn't have expected him to be such a responsible guy.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Yeah, I'm starting to see him in a different light, too!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Alright, let's go.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: We're the last ones. Everyone's waiting for us.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Mm-hm!

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: How come Gavial isn't back yet? She didn't get into trouble, did she?

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: Don't jinx it!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: She's here.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Now where is Avdotya? I'm eager to see the waterfall.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: You could go on ahead.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Now that won't do. This is a... how do you say this? Right, a historic moment!
A large crowd of Durins and Tiacauh have gathered in front of the mine.
They are all waiting for the last group to ride the elevator to the surface.
Wearing her usual smile, Gavial steps out with Stitch in tow.
She raises her right hand and greets the crowd, all of whom are beaming.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Today's a good day, everybody. Let's head to the lake for some fun!
Before she can finish her sentence, the crowd has already erupted in cheers.
Today, Acahualla is a tad bit more lively than before.
And in the future, it might get even livelier.
